passage: Supervisor's note, Friday. Observed: Pradeep, junior technician, spent last month shadowing Bindu on the repair bench. Bindu gave up several lunch hours to walk Pradeep through fault-finding. Today Pradeep handed Bindu a handwritten card and said, in front of the whole bench, "You taught me to trace the fault before touching the board. I want to do that for the new apprentice." Bindu looked embarrassed and pleased and said it was nothing. Pradeep has already run one short session with the apprentice this week, using Bindu's checklist, and asked me whether the studio could spare both of them an hour on Fridays. What I did: agreed to the hour and told Bindu what Pradeep had said. 🙂 Chaitanya

qa.q: What did Pradeep hand to Bindu?
qa.a: Pradeep handed Bindu a handwritten card.

qa.q: What did Bindu's embarrassed and pleased look suggest?
qa.a: Bindu was touched by the thanks but modest about it, saying it was nothing.

qa.q: What step did the supervisor take to support the mentoring?
qa.a: The supervisor agreed to an hour on Fridays for Pradeep and the apprentice, and told Bindu what Pradeep had said.

qa.q: How might the new apprentice benefit from Pradeep's plan?
qa.a: The apprentice gets short sessions using Bindu's checklist, so what Bindu taught is passed on.

grounding: A supervisor's note shows a junior thanking a mentor sincerely, applying what was taught, and passing it on to an apprentice.

passage:
In the small ITI in Mapusa, Francis had spent two years learning refrigeration repair from Sharmila ma'am. She had stayed back on Saturdays, unpaid, to help him with the wiring diagrams he couldn't read. When he failed the first practical, she said, "Again," and sat with him till dark.

Now he had his own small repair shop by the market. The first month's profit was tiny, but it was his.

He wanted to repay her and didn't know how. Money would insult her. So he went to the ITI with a box of bebinca and said, plainly, "Ma'am, everything I know is from you. Thank you."

She smiled and brushed it off. "Show me your shop."

When she came, a nervous boy was sweeping the floor: Rohit, a first-year ITI student. "I'm teaching him on Saturdays," Francis said. "Like you taught me."

Sharmila ma'am looked at the boy for a long moment, then at Francis. Her eyes were wet.

qa.q: What did Francis bring to the ITI?
qa.a: He brought a box of bebinca.

qa.q: What was Francis feeling as he thanked Sharmila ma'am?
qa.a: Francis felt deeply grateful and eager to repay her, but unsure how.

qa.q: How did Francis repay his mentor in the best way?
qa.a: By thanking her sincerely, using what she taught to build his shop, and passing it on by teaching Rohit on Saturdays.

qa.q: How might Sharmila ma'am have felt seeing Rohit in the shop?
qa.a: She was likely deeply moved and proud, seeing her teaching carried forward.

grounding: The passage shows a young man grateful to a mentor who guided him for hours, who thanks her sincerely, applies what she taught and passes it on to another learner.

passage:
In a bicycle workshop in Barcelona, Kaito had spent three years learning from Pablo, a grey-haired mechanic who explained every spoke and bearing as if it were a poem. Pablo had taken him in when Kaito spoke almost no Spanish, and had never once made him feel slow.

Now Kaito had been offered his own shop in Valencia. On his last evening he stood by the workbench, trying to find the words.

"Pablo, I don't know how to pay you back."

Pablo waved a greasy hand. "Pay me back? Don't be silly."

"Then tell me what you'd want."

Pablo thought. "When some kid comes into your shop who can't speak the language and doesn't know a wrench from a spoon, you teach him. Slowly. That's all."

Kaito nodded, his throat tight. Six months later, in Valencia, a young man from Senegal asked for work. Kaito handed him a wrench and said, "Slowly. We start with the spokes."

qa.q: Where was Kaito offered his own shop?
qa.a: He was offered his own shop in Valencia.

qa.q: What was Kaito feeling on his last evening at the workbench?
qa.a: Kaito felt deeply grateful and emotional, his throat tight, wanting to repay Pablo.

qa.q: What did Pablo ask for, and why is it the best repayment?
qa.a: He asked Kaito to teach a newcomer patiently, because passing on what you learned helps another person grow.

qa.q: How might the young man from Senegal feel starting at Kaito's shop?
qa.a: He may feel nervous but welcomed, given patient teaching just as Kaito once was.

grounding: The passage shows a young man grateful to a mentor who spent years guiding him, who thanks him sincerely and repays him by teaching another newcomer.
